transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2027-05-06 15:30 UTC | Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Amara (Redwood AE), Jonah (Redwood SE), Taylor (Redwood Partnerships), Miguel (Galaxion Head of Edge), Priya (Galaxion CTO), Lena (Partner Ops), Omar (Galaxion SE), Ravi (Galaxion Sales)

Summary: Intro + technical discovery, high-level commercial discussion, next steps captured as action items.

--- Topics / Quick bullets ---
- Embedding Redwood Private on Galaxion edge appliance (air-gapped option)
- Kernel compatibility and quantization (FP16, int8 paths)
- KMS/HSM + SSO/SAML + audit logs for regulated customers
- Benchmarks: p95 latency targets, throughput per-device, token cost tradeoffs
- Reseller vs OEM revenue split, pilot procurement path

--- Transcript (timestamps approximate, auto-transcribed, some errors expected) ---
[00:00] Amara (Redwood): hey everyone, thanks for carving time. quick intros from our side — i'm amara, i'm the AE here, our SE jonah and partnerships Taylor are on. how are you all?
[00:12] Miguel (Galaxion): good thanks, miguel here. we run the appliance biz, excited to talk about integrating a inference runtime like Redwood's. we've had inquiries from telco customers wanting low-latency llm routing at the edge.
[00:25] Priya (Galaxion): priya here, CTO. main thing for us is can we run this in a constrained edge profile? power/thermals matter, and customers need deterministic latency.
[00:38] Jonah (Redwood): great, thanks. quick note — on the Redwood side we have three modes: hosted api, dedicated, and private. for edge/offline customers we usually look at Redwood Private with a private control plane or an air-gapped bundle. question for you: are you thinking reseller (we ship appliance + sw) or OEM embed?
[01:05] Ravi (Galaxion): both, but first reseller pilots. prove performance with a few tier-1 customers, then talk OEM.
[01:12] Amara: perfect. jonah, i think you wanted to go through kernel and quantization constraints?
[01:17] Jonah: yep. so typical models we see in edge use-cases are trimmed-down decoder stacks — but the important bit is kernel support. do you run CUDA, paas drivers, or do you have a custom runtime on the cards?
[01:31] Omar (Galaxion): our appliance uses a custom lightweight hypervisor, exposes a passthrough for the ada-ish accelerators. we call the driver layer "galax-driver" — it's not stock cuda in all cases. we do support a CUDA shim for certain customers, but many run a vendor-supplied binary.
[01:48] Jonah: ok, that explains some of the variance we've seen. Redwood's runtime can work with CUDA, ROCm, and also some vendor-specific kernels if we compile with the right toolchain. we also have int8 and fp16 paths — but int8 needs per-kernel calibration and sometimes custom kernels. that's where we may hit friction.
[02:12] Priya: by calibration, do you mean we need to run a dataset through the model to generate scales? customers will balk at lengthy calibration steps in the field.
[02:22] Jonah: correct, typically we run a short calibration pass on representative prompts; it can be automated into the deployment pipeline, but it does mean we need a test corpus and a window to run it. for low-touch installs we can pre-calc profiles if the hardware and model are static.
[02:36] Miguel: what about kv cache and multi-turn? telco use-cases expect chat-like sessions with cached contexts.
[02:44] Jonah: we support persistent KV caching and prefix-cache to avoid re-computation. caveat: on-disk encrypted cache vs in-memory differs per appliance — do you have NVRAM or fast local SSD?
[02:55] Omar: we ship with an NVMe 2 TB by default and optional battery-backed NVRAM. encryption at rest is a must for the customers.
[03:04] Amara: good to know. let's pivot to security — SSO, KMS, and audit. priya, what are your customers asking for?
[03:12] Priya: SAML SSO, role-based access, tenant separation, and option for HSM-backed key management for model keys and encryption. also comprehensive audit logs for queries — some carriers need 7 years retention which is absurd but true.
[03:28] Taylor (Redwood): on the partner ops side we support SAML SSO, RBAC, and can integrate with external KMS/HSM via standard PKCS11 or cloud KMS endpoints if the appliance has connectivity. for air-gapped installs, our private package can be configured to point to a local HSM.
[03:45] Miguel: does that require code changes? we try to avoid touching our appliance firmware once certified.
[03:51] Jonah: mostly configuration. for HSM integration we sometimes need to build the agent with a PKCS11 binding. that's a one-time compile and packaging step; Taylor can help coordinate.
[04:03] Priya: i'm concerned about model provenance and model licensing — some open models have restrictive clauses around commercial use. how does Redwood handle a model catalog and signing?
[04:15] Amara: we publish a curated model catalog and a verified performance profile. for private deployments we can ship specific model binaries and maintain a signed manifest and versions. we also support pinning model hashes for reproducible rollouts.
[04:29] Ravi: commercial — if we go reseller, how do margins look? are you thinking rev-share or discounted OEM sku?
[04:36] Taylor: initial pilots usually run on a reseller discount + pilot credits; for scale OEM we discuss embedded licensing or per-device seat. we'll sketch a commercial framework.
[04:45] Miguel: sounds fair. technical bit — can we do warm boot of caches across reboots? some appliances reboot nightly for maintenance, we need to pre-warm model's kv cache to avoid cold-start spikes.
[04:56] Jonah: yes, we have snapshot/resume for KV caches. you can snapshot cache to disk and reload on boot, though it's not instantaneous. depends on size — huge contexts will still take time. we also have pre-warm hooks to replay a small set of prompts on startup.
[05:12] Priya: ok. let's talk about bench targets. what p95 latency should we aim for on a single Galaxion appliance for 8k context?
[05:21] Jonah: goal would be p95 200-400 ms for small instruction-response models at 2–4 tokens/sec encoding, but for 8k context and larger models it's more like 700ms-2s depending on quantization and kernel availability. we'll need to run real benchmarks to say definitively.
[05:39] Miguel: that range is broad but helpful. for telco LLM assistants, latency under 1s is a product requirement in many cases.
[05:47] Amara: this is where our lab session will help — we propose a 2-hour bench: 1) baseline with fp16, 2) int8 with calibration, 3) cache warm tests, 4) scale with concurrent sessions.
[06:00] Ravi: procurement — enough talk. how does the pilot purchase process work?
[06:06] Lena: internally we need an SOW and PO path. i'll coordinate with procurement once we have the rough SOW and price.
[06:12] Amara: we'll draft a light SOW after the bench.
[06:16] Jonah: a few gotchas i've seen — vendor-specific kernels sometimes mis-report memory usage; you might see OOMs in stress tests even when hardware is underutilized. we want to test kernel telemetry and instrumentation. do you expose low-level metrics?
[06:31] Omar: yes, we export telemetry (temperature, power, mem usage) via an agent to a local prometheus. we can add Redwood tracing hooks if needed.
[06:39] Jonah: perfect. that helps us map kernel behavior to observed metrics.
[06:43] Miguel: regulatory — some clients need data residency per country and audit. can Redwood support per-tenant keystore and localized logs?
[06:52] Amara: yes, Redwood Private supports per-tenant separation and you can configure log retention windows per customer. we can also push logs to local syslog collectors.
[06:59] Priya: one more security ask — can we run the control plane in Galaxion's network but Redwood manage updates out-of-band? basically remote managed but not broad external inbound.
[07:12] Taylor: we offer a private control plane that connects outbound to Redwood over an authenticated channel. for air-gapped installs we can ship an on-prem control plane that your team runs. both options available.
[07:25] Ravi: what about support SLAs for appliance customers? telcos expect 24/7 with fast escalation.
[07:31] Amara: enterprise support add-on includes 24/7 pager on-call, escalation to SEs, and on-site support in some cases. we can discuss a joint support model with Galaxion field engineers.
[07:42] Miguel: great. any previous partner integrations like this?
[07:46] Taylor: yes, we've done similar with a couple edge hardware vendors — we learned to standardize a "partner quickstart" which has three parts: kernel matrix, calibration harness, and a packaging/air-gap checklist.
[07:58] Priya: can you share that quickstart?
[08:00] Amara: yes, that's one of the action items.
[08:03] (brief cross-talk)
[08:10] Jonah: small technical note — model sharding across multiple small accelerators is non-trivial; if you plan to scale by stitching multiple cards, we need to look at network topology and NVLink-like interconnects or we accept model-split performance hits.
[08:26] Omar: our units can be clustered with a fast interconnect, but running a single large model across them adds complexity. most customers prefer per-device pinned models.
[08:36] Miguel: let's consider per-device pinned models first. lower complexity.
[08:40] Amara: sounds good. quick commercial question — any channel restrictions on selling bundled HW+SW?
[08:46] Ravi: no, but we want margin and simple procurement.
[08:49] Taylor: we'll propose a reseller discount and a pilot credit model.
[08:53] Amara: ok. wrapping toward next steps — we should align on artifacts to exchange. jonah, list the technical artifacts you need.
[09:02] Jonah: kernel/driver compatibility matrix, hardware spec sheet (power/thermals, memory, nvme), sample firmware images if possible, access to a small corpus for calibration, and prometheus metric endpoints or docs.
[09:14] Miguel: we'll share those. also we can provide a loaner unit for the lab if you want remote access.
[09:20] Jonah: a loaner would be ideal. remote access preferred, but an on-site loaner for the bench is ok.
[09:27] Priya: timeline — we want a pilot we can ship to a customer in Q3. is that realistic?
[09:33] Amara: yes, Q3 pilot is reasonable if we move quickly on benching and SOW.
[09:39] Ravi: pricing sense — for pilots, are there credits vs seat fees?
[09:42] Amara: pilots usually run as a discounted reseller bundle + pilot credits for compute. we'll put numbers in the commercial sketch.
[09:48] (silence, note-taking)
[09:55] Jonah: one more technical caveat — some models have ops not supported by smaller accelerators (e.g., FlashAttention variants). if the model uses these ops we may need to fallback to CPU for specific kernels which hurts latency. we'll test for that.
[10:12] Priya: can you give an example of an ops mismatch?
[10:15] Jonah: sure — some fused attention kernels expect certain shared memory sizes; if the hardware scheduler doesn't support the fusion we see slow-paths. it's technical but important for perf.
[10:27] Miguel: noted. okay let's capture who does what and by when.
[10:31] Amara: recap of actions — jonah share matrix, miguel share firmware/specs, amara share security artifacts, taylor draft commercial. bench scheduled tentative week of 5/17.
[10:45] Lena: i'll send calendar availability and procurement contacts.
[10:48] Amara: perfect. any final q's?
[10:51] Priya: only — do you have references of similar integrations we can peek at?
[10:55] Taylor: yes, we'll anonymize and share a short case note.
[10:58] Miguel: thanks everyone, great convo. looking forward to the bench.
[11:02] Amara: thanks all, we'll follow up with artifacts and SOW draft.
[11:08] (meeting ends)
